ATLAS-2 MAINTENANCE AND CAPACITY UPGRADE REPORT V1.0

1. Summary

The Atlas-2 maintenance window took place on 12 and 13 September 2026. It included storage expansion, updates to the base system, GPU drivers, the queue service, monitoring, and backup verification.

Usable capacity increased from 84 TB to 196 TB. Twelve disks, two enclosures, and an additional controller were installed. The configuration tolerates two disk failures in every group. Read, write, simulated-failure, and restoration tests completed successfully.

Service became available again on 13 September at 18:10. Two research jobs resumed from checkpoints, and one was rerun. No project information was lost.

2. Scope

The intervention covered CPU nodes, three GPUs, working storage, archive storage, authentication, queues, monitoring, and backups. Access groups and quotas were not changed without a specific request.

3. Preparation

Before the window, users were notified, new submissions stopped, backups verified, and active jobs recorded. Configurations and versions were exported. The rollback plan was tested on an integration node.

4. Changes

The base system was updated to the approved version. GPU drivers were updated in a way compatible with libraries used by ARIADNA and LUMEN. The queue service received fixes for limits and resumption. Monitoring added capacity, temperature, SMART errors, and backup status.

Maintenance record 29

Restoration of an ARIADNA sample, a LUMEN collection, and a VERDANT aggregate confirmed permissions, checksums, and timing. Restored files were deleted after comparison.

Maintenance record 30

Quotas were reviewed so that new capacity did not remove usage controls. The increase was allocated by project through justified requests while retaining operational headroom.

Maintenance record 31

The window closed with zero critical failures, one recommendation to automate SMART tests, and another to better document checkpoints for long-running jobs.
